reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that standard eSports metrics like kills and deaths fail to capture nuanced contributions to team outcomes. Smart kills are those that meaningfully shift win probability, while worthless deaths are those that decrease it. These are modeled as stochastic processes where each action is a random variable with a conditional distribution over win probability. The smart kill differential S_k - W_d serves as a proxy for net contribution. The action efficiency tensor E_ij encodes how efficiently each action type contributes to team objectives, derived from granular telemetry. The conditional win probability P(W|X) is a Bayesian belief update over the set of observed actions X. These primitives form a coherent framework for quantifying individual impact in team-based digital sports.
